summary:
The lcmodel investigation is finished. It uses the newest complete rerun (lcmodel/v6, which supersedes v5: same code, but the main-sequence table is smoothed so it leaves no artificial edges in the mass posterior). I added checks in lcmodel/v7rep.

MAIN RESULT: the TESS light curve on its own does not fix how much of the light comes from the eclipsing pair. It only sets a lower limit: f_EB > 2.5% (dchi2 < 4) or > 2.2% (dchi2 < 9). Injection tests confirm that limit.

Once the pair is required to be main-sequence stars, there is a single solution and the converged MCMC gives:
- an M2V primary (M1 = 0.44 +- 0.025 Msun, R1 = 0.483 +- 0.012 Rsun) and an M4.5V secondary (M2 = 0.19 +- 0.014, R2 = 0.213 +- 0.009);
- nearly central eclipses (b = 0.10, 95% < 0.22; i = 89.1 deg);
- f_EB = 2.82 +- 0.20% of the TESS flux, and J = 0.523 +- 0.012, i.e. T2/T1 = 0.89;
- a main-sequence photometric distance of 252 (+27/-24) pc (95% 207-305 pc), against 297 pc for the G star.
Putting the main-sequence pair exactly at the G-star distance ('bound' fit) costs only dchi2 = +0.55 (M1 0.47 +- 0.014, f_EB 2.70%).

A sceptic will find one caveat. With e sin w free and uniform priors, the light curve mildly prefers more light from the pair (posterior L3 0.932, f_EB 6.8 +- 1.3%). That preference rests entirely on e sin w = +0.030 +- 0.014:
- Fixing e sin w = 0, which is expected for a 1.3-d M-dwarf binary, makes the profile flat (dchi2 <= 1 for L3 0.88-0.97, minimum at 0.96).
- An injection with true L3 = 0.972 is recovered at 0.968 by the same sampler.
- The out-of-eclipse ellipsoidal limit (< 74 ppm) and the measured red colour of the eclipsed star rule out the main-sequence versions of the lower-L3 solutions.
Out of eclipse there is also spot modulation at exactly P_EB (280-480 ppm, 1-1.7% of the pair's light), so the M dwarfs rotate in step with their orbit.

ECLIPSE TIMING: a linear ephemeris is adequate (P = 1.30367228 d +- 0.016 s). Curvature is zero within errors (c = -0.001 +- 0.039 min/yr^2; |dP/dt| < 0.032 s/yr at 95%), and no light-travel-time signal is found (best dchi2 6.0, p = 0.37). Positive controls are recovered. Timing rules out the G star orbiting the pair at a <~ 10 au (>= 94% of orbits) and most orbits at <= 20 au (66%). It has no sensitivity at the 150-370 au projected separations allowed by the localisation.

CROSS-CHECKS: all results agree with the localisation result (M1.5-M2.5 primary, BP-RP 2.3, shallow-eclipse light BP-RP >~ 3, pair 1.5-3% of TESS light). They are marginally consistent with the 4040 K colour estimate: our M2V gives SuperWASP and W1 depth ratios within 1 sigma of the measured ones.

NET: the light-curve physics places the eclipsing M-dwarf pair at the G star's distance (to within 1.7 sigma), not in the distant background. That favours the bound triple. The light curve alone cannot tell a bound pair from an unrelated pair at the same distance; that needs the chance-alignment prior (about 4e-5 for any unrelated M dwarf within 1.24 arcsec, from the localisation task).

key_numbers.quantity: f_EB = 1 - L3, the pair's fraction of the TESS flux (main-sequence fit, L3 free)
key_numbers.method: v6 main-sequence-constrained emcee chain (chain_msfree.h5: 7059 iterations x 48 walkers, 30% burn-in, max tau 92 -> 77 tau, max R-hat 1.004, split-half shifts <= 0.14 sigma). Free: M1, q, dR1, dR2 ~ N(0, 0.07), dJ ~ N(0, 0.10), b0, L3 uniform, e cos w, e sin w, limb darkening, T0, P, 5 depth scales. Derived in v7rep/derived_msfree_b0.3.json
key_numbers.uncertainty: Statistical. About +-5% relative systematic from the product depth scale: L3 refers to the SPOC S68 PDCSAP flux, and S1/S28 primaries are 8% deeper. Prior-driven through the main-sequence assumption.

key_numbers.quantity: Lower limit on f_EB from light-curve shape alone (no main-sequence prior)
key_numbers.method: Profile likelihood in L3 (v6 profile_L3_default.json, 16 grid points, multi-start scaled L-BFGS-B over all other parameters). The edge is the b0 -> 0 (central eclipse) limit.
key_numbers.uncertainty: The edge is reproduced in all 3 injections: dchi2(0.975) = 6.8 and 11.5 for true L3 0.91 and 0.62. The true value 0.972 of injection A lies at dchi2 = 3.2, so use the dchi2 = 9 limit.

key_numbers.quantity: Upper side of f_EB from shape alone
key_numbers.value: Not constrained: dchi2 < 4 for L3 0.82-0.975 (f_EB 2.5-18%); dchi2 = 6.2 at L3 = 0 (with e free)
key_numbers.method: Same profile
key_numbers.uncertainty: Injections: true L3 0.62 gave a minimum at 0.90 and dchi2(true) 1.8; true 0.91 gave 0.94 and 0.18; true 0.972 gave 0.965 and 3.2. The location of the minimum is therefore not a measurement.

key_numbers.quantity: L3 profile with e sin w fixed at 0
key_numbers.method: Targeted re-optimisation, new in this run (v7rep/prof_esin0.py, prof_esin0_summary.json). Same likelihood and optimiser; e cos w left free.
key_numbers.uncertainty: Single-point optimisations with 4 seeds each. Several solutions reach the edges of the limb-darkening prior box (u1a ~ 0.6, u1b ~ 0.05).

key_numbers.quantity: Geometric posterior with uniform priors (no main-sequence prior)
key_numbers.method: The v6 c03 chain (stopped at 1898 iterations) resumed on a copy to 15036 iterations x 56 walkers (v7rep/chain_geoext.h5). 50% burn-in; tau 230 (65 tau in total, 33 after burn-in); R-hat <= 1.009
key_numbers.uncertainty: L3 drifted from 0.955 to 0.932 over the first ~6000 iterations and was stable afterwards. NOT adopted: it depends on e sin w ~ 0.03 (see the e sin w = 0 profile), and its main-sequence versions are excluded by the ellipsoidal limit and by the eclipsed star's colour.

key_numbers.quantity: Geometric posterior for injection A (true L3 0.972, k 0.46, b0 0.10, rsum 0.162, J 0.52, e = 0)
key_numbers.method: Same sampler set-up on the injection data set: synthetic EB multiplied into the real light curves at phase 0.25 (v7rep/geo_injA.py; 16097 iterations, n/tau 102, R-hat 1.002)
key_numbers.uncertainty: One noise realisation. It shows a true L3 near 0.97 is NOT pulled to 0.93 by prior volume.

key_numbers.quantity: Radius ratio k = R2/R1
key_numbers.value: 0.441 +- 0.018 (95% 0.407-0.475) with the main-sequence prior; shape alone allows 0.18-0.47 (dchi2 < 4)
key_numbers.method: Main-sequence chain; profile
key_numbers.uncertainty: Degenerate with L3 and b0 (correlation with L3 +0.94). The value is set by the main-sequence prior.

key_numbers.quantity: Impact parameter b0 = a cos i / (R1+R2)
key_numbers.method: Main-sequence chain
key_numbers.uncertainty: Shape alone allows 0-0.64 (dchi2 < 4). Value driven by the main-sequence prior.

key_numbers.quantity: Surface-brightness ratio J and temperature ratio
key_numbers.value: J = 0.523 +- 0.012. T2/T1 = 0.887 +- 0.004 (blackbody in the TESS band at T1 = 3510 K); 0.90 +- 0.01 from the main-sequence relation. J stays 0.44-0.52 over the whole dchi2 < 4 profile
key_numbers.method: Main-sequence chain; profile
key_numbers.uncertainty: Robust: weakly dependent on L3.

key_numbers.quantity: Fractional radii
key_numbers.method: Main-sequence chain
key_numbers.uncertainty: Shape alone allows r1 0.110-0.168 (dchi2 < 4).

key_numbers.quantity: e cos w
key_numbers.value: 0.00070 +- 0.00034 (light-curve fit). From the ETV secondary offset of +0.77 +- 0.55 min (+46 +- 33 s): 0.00064 +- 0.00046. The expected Roemer delay (2a/c)(M1-M2)/(M1+M2) is about +8 s, leaving +38 +- 33 s, i.e. e cos w ~ 0.0005 +- 0.0005
key_numbers.method: Main-sequence chain; linear ETV fit with a separate secondary offset
key_numbers.uncertainty: Consistent with 0 at <= 1.7 sigma.

key_numbers.quantity: e sin w
key_numbers.value: 0.013 +- 0.009 (main-sequence chain); 0.030 +- 0.014 (geometric chain); -0.007 to +0.041 along the L3 profile. Fixing e = 0 completely costs dchi2 = +4.6 for 2 parameters (p ~ 0.10)
key_numbers.method: Chains; v6 variants_a.json
key_numbers.uncertainty: Correlated with limb darkening (r = -0.46 with u1a) and with L3. Prior-sensitive; consistent with a circular orbit.

key_numbers.quantity: Component masses, radii, temperatures and types (main-sequence fit, L3 free)
key_numbers.method: Main-sequence chain (masses come from the light-curve density and J under the main-sequence relations; there is no dynamical mass)
key_numbers.uncertainty: Prior-driven by the main-sequence assumption, with 7% radius and 10% J nuisance priors. A wider-prior maximum-likelihood fit still gives M1 0.43-0.45 (L3 0.959-0.971). Only one mode: other starts end >= 85 worse in chi2.

key_numbers.quantity: Main-sequence fit with the pair placed at the G-star distance (bound)
key_numbers.value: M1 = 0.470 +- 0.014, M2 = 0.207 +- 0.012, Teff1 = 3585 +- 38 K, f_EB = 2.70% (+0.20/-0.16), dmag = -0.07 +- 0.10. Maximum-likelihood chi2 only +0.55 worse than the free main-sequence fit
key_numbers.method: v6 chain_msbound.h5: 7004 iterations x 48 walkers, n/tau 70, R-hat <= 1.006. f_EB fixed by the pair's main-sequence M_T at mu = 7.37, A_T = 0.02, Tmag 11.358, with an N(0, 0.15 mag) offset dmag
key_numbers.uncertainty: The dmag posterior is mostly the prior (0.10 vs 0.15).

key_numbers.quantity: Photometric distance of the main-sequence pair implied by f_EB
key_numbers.method: Main-sequence chain plus TIC-8 T(G, BP-RP) main-sequence absolute magnitudes
key_numbers.uncertainty: Plus ~0.07-0.15 mag systematic from the main-sequence relation scatter and inflation (~7%), and ~+-2.5% in distance from the depth-scale systematic.

key_numbers.quantity: Predicted near-IR contrast if the pair is at 297 pc
key_numbers.value: dKs(pair - blend) = 2.80 +- 0.15 (free main-sequence fit); 2.62 +- 0.08 (bound fit)
key_numbers.method: Main-sequence M_Ks
key_numbers.uncertainty: Main-sequence relation

key_numbers.quantity: Eclipse depths
key_numbers.value: Diluted primary 5770 +- 100 ppm, secondary 2600 +- 55 ppm. Undiluted 20.5 +- 1.4% and 9.3 +- 0.7% (main-sequence fit). Primary depth scale relative to the template: SPOC1 1.083 +- 0.029, SPOC28 1.081 +- 0.024, SPOC68 0.994 +- 0.031, TC95 0.986 +- 0.027, TC105 0.981 +- 0.024, TC106 1.020 +- 0.028
key_numbers.method: Chain plus v6 c06 per-product depth fits with injection-bootstrap errors
key_numbers.uncertainty: The 8% S1/S28 vs S68 difference is a product/crowding systematic.

key_numbers.quantity: Ellipsoidal (cos 4 pi phi) amplitude
key_numbers.value: -8 +- 37 ppm (diluted); one-sided 95% upper limit 74 ppm. The main-sequence solution predicts 21 (18-27) ppm. At L3 = 0.92-0.955 the main-sequence-consistent q ~ 0.8 predicts 87-235 ppm (excluded). L3 <= 0.90 would require q < 0.2 (q < 0.08 at L3 <= 0.82), which cannot produce J ~ 0.4-0.48
key_numbers.method: Per-sector harmonic fits with a spline baseline (v6 e01), DerSimonian-Laird random-effects combination over 6 sectors (tau = 78 ppm between sectors), Student-t; Morris & Naftilan alpha = 1.30 (x0.86 when computing the limit). Recomputed over the full profile: v7rep/ellipsoidal_fullprofile.json
key_numbers.uncertainty: Spot harmonics leak into cos 4 pi phi; the 15% uncertainty in alpha is included conservatively.

key_numbers.quantity: Out-of-eclipse spot modulation at P_EB
key_numbers.value: 280-480 ppm semi-amplitude in each of 6 sectors (1.0-1.7% of the pair's light). The global Lomb-Scargle peak falls within 0.05 resolution elements of P_EB in 5/6 sectors (binomial p ~ 9e-9). The phase changes between sectors
key_numbers.method: v6 e01/e05: eclipse-masked, spline-detrended Lomb-Scargle and harmonic fits
key_numbers.uncertainty: Reflection and beaming cannot be separated from spots.

key_numbers.quantity: Linear ephemeris
key_numbers.method: Weighted fit to 187 primary + secondary times from template fits (v6 e02/e03). Errors calibrated per product by fake-phase injection, then scaled by 1.125 (linear chi2 before scaling 233/184)
key_numbers.uncertainty: Includes the 12.5% excess scatter (spots?). TESScut vs SPOC time systems agree to 16 +- 18 s.

key_numbers.quantity: Period change / curvature
key_numbers.value: c = -0.001 +- 0.039 min/yr^2 (|c| < 0.077 at 95%); dP/dt = -0.0005 +- 0.0165 s/yr (|dP/dt| < 0.032 s/yr); dchi2 (linear - quadratic) = 0.0008, null p 0.98. Line-of-sight acceleration |a_los| < 2.8e-6 m/s^2, equivalent to the G star at <= 47 au along the line of sight
key_numbers.method: Quadratic ephemeris; empirical null from 20000 synthetic sets. Positive controls with time warps applied at the light-curve level: injected 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5 min/yr^2 recovered 0.102 +- 0.040 / 0.249 +- 0.043 / 0.503 +- 0.054
key_numbers.uncertainty: Cubic (dchi2 2.2), separate primary/secondary quadratics (dchi2 2.1) and a separate secondary period (dchi2 1.25) are all insignificant and worse in BIC.

key_numbers.quantity: Light-travel-time (LTTE) limits
key_numbers.value: Best circular LTTE: P_out 907 d, A 2.1 min, dchi2 6.0, look-elsewhere p 0.37 (no detection). 95% upper limits on semi-amplitude: 1.4-3.4 min for P_out 0.5-11 yr (except aliases: 14.7 min near 1 yr, 9.3 min near 3.25 yr); 6.6 min at 14 yr, 14.5 at 19 yr, 33 at 26 yr
key_numbers.method: Period scan with a null distribution (v6 etvfit_default.json)
key_numbers.uncertainty: Calibrated against the null

key_numbers.quantity: Outer-companion (G star, 1.03 Msun) exclusion from ETVs
key_numbers.value: Fraction of random orbits (isotropic, e uniform 0-0.8) excluded at dchi2 > 9: 1 au 0.955, 2 au 0.98, 3-7 au >= 0.99, 10 au 0.94, 14 au 0.84, 20 au 0.66, 25 au 0.46, 30 au 0.30, 40 au 0.10, 50 au 0.05, 80 au 0.007, >= 160 au 0. With dchi2 > 4: 10 au 0.97, 20 au 0.77, 30 au 0.48, 50 au 0.10. Gaia RV constancy alone excludes 84-96% at 1-3 au
key_numbers.method: v6 e04 LTTE Monte Carlo (4000 orbits per a) against the measured O-C, with T0/P/secondary offset refitted; M_EB 0.6 (results unchanged within +-0.02 for M_EB 0.7-1.0, v5)
key_numbers.uncertainty: Monte Carlo +-0.01

key_numbers.quantity: Expected ETV curvature at the separations allowed by localisation
key_numbers.value: <= 0.003 min/yr^2 for 0.5 arcsec (150 au projected), about 27x below the 95% limit. Timing has no sensitivity at 150-370 au
key_numbers.method: Maximum line-of-sight acceleration 0.385 G M3 / s^2 converted with c = a/(2c_light)
key_numbers.uncertainty: Analytic

key_numbers.quantity: Injection recovery (main-sequence fit)
key_numbers.value: Injection A (truth L3 0.972, k 0.46, b0 0.10, rsum 0.162, J 0.52) recovered by the free main-sequence fit as L3 0.9714, k 0.460, b0 0.02, rsum 0.1615, J 0.525
key_numbers.method: v6 c07 maximum-likelihood fit on data_injA
key_numbers.uncertainty: Tests only the optimiser on a main-sequence-like truth. No main-sequence fits were run on the non-main-sequence truths B and C.

key_numbers.quantity: Chromatic consistency check
key_numbers.value: Predicted SuperWASP(V)/TESS and W1/TESS primary-depth ratios: M2V 0.28 and 3.56 (chi2 0.86 against the measured 0.42 +- 0.15 and 3.7 +- 1.1); M1V 0.32 and 3.26 (0.58); K7V 0.45 and 2.47 (1.31)
key_numbers.method: Pecaut & Mamajek colours relative to the blend V 11.9, T 11.358, W1 ~ 10.28 (v7rep/chromatic_check.py)
key_numbers.uncertainty: Ignores the exact SuperWASP passband and limb-darkening differences between bands.

conclusions.claim: The light-curve shape alone gives only a lower limit on the pair's share of the TESS light: f_EB > 2.2% (dchi2 9), > 2.5% (dchi2 4). It does not measure f_EB.
conclusions.evidence: L3 profile: dchi2 +3.8 at 0.975 (b0 hits 0), +19 at 0.983, +118 at 0.99. The edge appears in all 3 injections. The low side is flat (dchi2 6.2 at L3 = 0), and injections show the location of the minimum is biased (true 0.62 gives a minimum at 0.90).

conclusions.claim: Requiring main-sequence stars gives one well-defined, converged solution: an M2V (0.44 Msun, 0.48 Rsun) primary and an M4.5V (0.19 Msun, 0.21 Rsun) secondary with nearly central eclipses, f_EB = 2.8 +- 0.2%, J = 0.52 (T2/T1 0.89). k, b0, L3 and the masses are set by the prior; J, rsum, depths and timing are robust.
conclusions.evidence: Main-sequence chain n/tau 77, R-hat <= 1.004; one mode (other starts >= 85 worse in chi2); a wider-prior maximum-likelihood fit still gives M1 0.43-0.45; injection A recovered.

conclusions.claim: With e sin w free, the light curve's mild preference for more light from the pair (geometric L3 0.93, f_EB ~7%) is not physical: it rests on e sin w = +0.03 +- 0.014. Fixing e sin w = 0 makes the profile flat over L3 0.88-0.97 with its minimum at 0.96. The main-sequence values of these lower-L3 solutions are excluded by the ellipsoidal limit, and the eclipsed star's colour (BP-RP 2.3) argues against them.
conclusions.evidence: prof_esin0_summary.json; the injection-A geometric chain recovers 0.968 for a true 0.972; ellipsoidal limit 74 ppm vs 87-235 ppm predicted for q ~ 0.8 at L3 0.92-0.955. The free-e best fit is only dchi2 2.4 better than the e sin w = 0 fits.

conclusions.claim: The main-sequence pair implied by the light curve sits at about the G star's distance (252 +27/-24 pc vs 297 pc, 1.7 sigma), and a bound main-sequence pair at 297 pc fits equally well (dchi2 +0.55). A distant background EB does not fit: at f_EB >= 2.2%, an M-dwarf pair with the measured density (~3.9 rho_sun) cannot be much beyond ~310 pc.
conclusions.evidence: Distance posteriors from the main-sequence chains; the bound chain's dmag = -0.07 +- 0.10. This relies on main-sequence luminosities and on the main-sequence (or e = 0) choice for L3.

conclusions.claim: A linear ephemeris is adequate. There is no period change or LTTE over 2018-2025. Timing excludes the G star orbiting the pair at a <~ 10-15 au (>= 84-99% of orbits) but says nothing at the 150-370 au projected separations allowed by the localisation, so it cannot decide between bound and chance alignment.
conclusions.evidence: Quadratic dchi2 0.0008 (null p 0.98) with positive controls recovered; LTTE best p 0.37; companion Monte Carlo; expected curvature at 150 au <= 0.003 min/yr^2 vs the 0.077 limit.

conclusions.claim: The pair's M dwarfs rotate in step with the 1.30-d orbit, as expected for a tidally locked short-period M-dwarf binary. The modulation comes from the pair, not from the 5-Gyr G star.
conclusions.evidence: The Lomb-Scargle peak falls at P_EB in 5/6 sectors (p ~ 9e-9), 280-480 ppm with changing phase; no ellipsoidal signal is detected, consistent with the 21-ppm prediction.

conclusions.claim: The results agree with the localisation result and are within ~1 sigma of the archival colour data. Against the colour fit's 4040 K central value the agreement is marginal (~1.7 sigma).
conclusions.evidence: Predicted primary BP-RP 2.28 (2.19-2.36) vs 2.31 (2.22-2.40) from localisation; secondary BP-RP 3.1 vs >~3; f_EB 2.7-2.8% vs 1.5-3%. Teff1 3510-3585 K vs 4040 (+330/-280) K. An M2V eclipsed star predicts SuperWASP/TESS 0.28 and W1/TESS 3.56 vs the measured 0.42 +- 0.15 and 3.7 +- 1.1.

implications_bound_vs_background:
The light-curve physics does not support a chance-aligned BACKGROUND (distant) EB.

Under the main-sequence assumption, the measured density (r1 = 0.112, rho1 ~ 3.9 rho_sun) and J, together with the independent red colour of the eclipsed star (localisation BP-RP 2.3; archival depth ratios), make the eclipsing stars an M2V + M4.5V pair. Their share of the flux (f_EB = 2.8 +- 0.2%; the shape alone requires > 2.2%) puts them at 252 (+27/-24) pc (95% 207-305 pc). That is at the G star's 297 pc within 1.7 sigma. A main-sequence pair placed at exactly 297 pc fits the light curve as well (dchi2 +0.55, dmag -0.07 +- 0.10).

Two kinds of background pair fail:
- An M-dwarf pair at >~ 400 pc would contribute < 1.5% of the light, which the eclipse shape excludes at dchi2 > 9.
- Brighter background pairs (K/G types at larger distances) need lower-density primaries. Their main-sequence versions fail the ellipsoidal limit (q ~ 0.8 predicts 87-235 ppm vs < 74 ppm), and they would make the eclipsed light bluer than measured.

What the light curve cannot exclude is an UNRELATED M-dwarf pair at roughly the same distance, in front of or behind the G star. That depends on the chance-alignment prior: the localisation task estimates ~4e-5 for any unrelated M dwarf within 1.24 arcsec, and a 1.3-d eclipsing M-dwarf binary is rarer still.

Eclipse timing cannot help at the allowed separations. It rules out only a tight (<~ 10-15 au) orbit of the G star, which localisation and Gaia already disfavour. The absence of curvature is exactly what a bound companion at 150-370 au would show.

On balance the light-curve results favour a bound hierarchical triple: a 5-Gyr G2V star with an M2V+M4.5V eclipsing binary at a few hundred au. The M dwarfs are probably slightly inflated (dR1 = +6 +- 3.5%), as is common in short-period M-dwarf EBs. Confirming it needs high-resolution imaging (predicted dKs ~ 2.6-2.8 at <~ 1 arcsec), a common proper motion, or spectroscopy of the M-dwarf lines.
caveats:
1) Prior-driven quantities: L3/f_EB, k, b0, M1, M2, R1, R2, Teff1/2 and the spectral types all come from imposing main-sequence relations (smoothed Pecaut & Mamajek, with 7% radius and 10% J nuisance priors). None is a dynamical measurement. The light curve alone constrains only J, rsum, the depths, e cos w (timing) and the upper limit on L3. Limb darkening is prior-driven: u1 spans the 0.05-0.60 box, and several fits sit on its edges. e sin w is correlated with limb darkening.

2) The uniform-prior geometric posterior (L3 0.932, f_EB 6.8 +- 1.3%) disagrees with the main-sequence value. I trace this to e sin w ~ 0.03 (fixing e sin w = 0 removes it) and argue it is unphysical. A referee could still argue for inflated, possibly young M dwarfs with f_EB ~ 5-8%. That would put a pair with main-sequence luminosities at ~160-200 pc, i.e. not bound. The case for f_EB ~ 2.8% rests on four things: a circular orbit, main-sequence radii within ~7-10%, the ellipsoidal limit, and the localisation colour.

3) Injection tests use one noise realisation per truth (A 0.972, B 0.91, C 0.62). Main-sequence fits were run on injections only for truth A (main-sequence-like), so prior-driven bias on non-main-sequence truths is untested. The geometric-chain injection is new here (v7rep).

4) Chains: the v6 main-sequence chains were interrupted before writing metadata. I rebuilt the metadata from c07_msfit.py (v7rep/chain_ms*_meta.json); both chains converged at ~7000 iterations. The v6 geometric chain was interrupted at 1898 iterations; I resumed a copy to 15036. After burn-in it covers 33 tau with R-hat 1.009, but it was drifting during the first ~6000 iterations. The v5 chain (unsmoothed main-sequence table) gave M1 0.417 with an artificial edge at 0.398; it is superseded.

5) The e sin w = 0 profile has only 6 points, one optimisation each with 4 seeds; it is not an MCMC.

6) Depth scales differ by 8% between SPOC S1/S28 and S68 (crowding or aperture). f_EB refers to S68 PDCSAP, so add about +-5% relative systematic.

7) ETV errors needed a 12.5% inflation (linear chi2 233/184), possibly spot-induced timing noise; all limits use the inflated errors. The LTTE limits have aliases near 1 and 3.25 yr. The companion Monte Carlo assumes isotropic orientations and e uniform in 0-0.8.

8) The photometric distance assumes main-sequence absolute magnitudes for the fitted masses (scatter ~0.06 mag plus inflation effects) and A_T = 0.02.

9) The chromatic comparison is approximate (P&M colours, V band used for SuperWASP).

10) The out-of-eclipse amplitudes vary between sectors (spots), so the ellipsoidal limit uses a random-effects model. The alpha coefficient is uncertain by ~15%.
